newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas called unchanged amid light OTC trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas called unchanged amid light OTC trade.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open on either side of unchanged Thursday following light over-the-counter trading, industry sources said.

December OTC business ranged from about $2.85 to $2.87. Most traders said they anticipated trading to be fairly range-bound throughout Thursday's session as few signals were expected from the cash market on the last day of the month.
In Wednesday's ACCESS session, December last traded 1.3 cents lower at $2.851 after hitting a contract high of $2.88 earlier.

American Gas Association said Wednesday that U.S. gas inventories rose last week by 34 billion cubic feet (bcf) to 85 percent of capacity, still 256 bcf or nine percent below year-ago levels. Eastern stocks climbed to 95 percent full, about even with last year, while producing region storage at 73 percent still lagged 1995 by 16 points.

Traders said they saw some support in December at $2.77, then the $2.66 area. Resistance was first pegged at the $2.88 contract high and then at $2.92 and $2.98, two prominent spot continuation highs set in late June and early July.

On Wednesday, November cash prices on the Midcontinent pipes gained another 10 cents to the mid-to-high $2.70s, though trading was sparse. Early price indications for November 2 gas flows on the Gulf Coast pipes were also stronger in the low-$2.80s.

Forecasters were calling for a continuation of well below-normal temperatures in most of the Midwest through the weekend, while in the Northeast, the thermometer is expected to gradually drop, landing at five to 10 degrees below-normal on Saturday.
